request: Compare the intermittent instance-connection failure with matching-version TrinityCore on GitHub first, then other Legion projects; repair an evidenced missing stage if found.

references.version_evidence: Commit explicitly updates allowed build to 7.3.5.26972; the WorldSocket.cpp history through 2018-08-12 still identifies this as its latest change.

references.scope: Pinned Legion branch with matching initializer/authentication/ConnectTo wire representation. Ashamane is based on TrinityCore, not independent confirmation from a different networking design.
Original threading-model change explicitly explains per-network-thread io_service and single-thread ownership of socket operations except the intermediate packet queue.

same: Server and client initializer lines, each 48 wire bytes including newline
ConnectTo payload/envelope field order, RSA protocol key equality, public protocol HMAC constant, Pi digits, Haiku, Panama key, Adler and XOR constants
comparison.difference: Both pinned upstream implementations queue an asynchronous IP query in Start and initialize buffers/read/greeting in CheckIpCallback, dispatched by the socket network thread's Update. Our Start instead ran synchronous SQL and issued the native read and non-locking greeting write from SocketMgr's acceptor thread; the async handoff was commented out.
comparison.proved: The pinned pre-fix production Start, executed with the real Socket/MessageBuffer in a two-thread fixture, issued read/write on the acceptor thread. The same fixture can complete its greeting successfully; it does not reproduce or prove the cause of the user's silent connection.
comparison.not_proved: No dynamic failed-client trace identifies which client receive/dispatch branch stopped responding. The upstream handoff difference is a concrete architecture divergence, not proof of a race causing the observed sent=48/received=0 incident.
comparison.excluded_differences: Do not replace the 7.3.5 initializer with modern TrinityCore V2, change authentication bytes, remove the working fresh-accept-socket repair, or remove bounded retry/deadline/lifetime fixes.

WorldSocket.cpp: Restore asynchronous IP query scheduling in Start and network-thread initialization in CheckIpCallback via the existing QueryCallbackProcessor/Update dispatcher.
Reject a result for an already closed/closing socket before starting reads or queuing a greeting.

Adapt the callback to this core's actual SELECT * FROM ip_banned result: a nonempty result remains a ban. Do not read the IP string/timestamp as upstream's differently shaped ban-status/country projection.
Initialize send-buffer size to 4096 as upstream does; SocketAdded retains its configured override.
implementation.LoginDatabase.cpp: Register LOGIN_SEL_IP_INFO with CONNECTION_BOTH: asynchronous world sockets and existing synchronous bnetserver callers are both supported; query text/schema/ban semantics are unchanged.
unchanged: Twelve-second retry deadline and five-attempt bound

automated_checks: compare_legion_handshake.py against both pinned references: initializer, auth packet layouts, ConnectTo constants/crypto and serial checks pass; baseline active_start parser excludes commented-out AsyncQuery text.
Test-WorldSocketStartThread.ps1 -Baseline: actual pre-fix Start runs read/write on acceptor; successful exact loopback exchange also demonstrates the distinction from reproducing the user's failure.

Test-WorldSocketStartThread.ps1: actual current Start/CheckIpCallback, native Socket/MessageBuffer and native QueryCallback/AsyncCallbackProcessor with controlled database futures: 16 worker-owned exact exchanges; pending future, banned result and close-before-result paths pass. No live account or database mutation.
Test-HandshakeDeadline.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary: actual timeout/cancellation, ordinary EOF, young/authenticated sockets, detach and already-closed cases pass.
Test-InstanceConnectRetry.ps1: retry bounds, silent-client deadlines, queued/stale reports, successful/cancelled login and link guards pass.
Test-WorldSocketDiagnostics.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary: Windows TCP_INFO ABI/counters and closed-socket fallback pass; all five deployed diagnostic call sites remain present.

verify_world_socket_start_release.py: actual PE Start calls async SQL, binds CheckIpCallback and does not issue native reads/greeting writes; Update dispatches ready queries and the bound callback issues native read/write.
Game and database libraries built in original generated Release locations, followed by staging-only final worldserver link. Canonical EXE/MAP copies have matching hashes.
Test-ScepterLogin.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary and the existing ten scenario completion/exit/relog/persistence PE call paths pass.

Canonical startup reached ready without ERROR or DBErrors entries. Sixteen initializer-only probes against the real MariaDB-backed canonical server, instance listener first, received exact 48-byte greetings and valid 55-byte challenges on both 8086 and 8085 (31-47ms). These exercise actual asynchronous prepared-query completion; they send no account authentication.

deployment.ownership: User worldserver had already shut down before deployment. No user-owned process was stopped. Owned hidden validation worldserver 26944 reached ready and shut down gracefully with exit code 0; no temporary server remains.
deployment.preserved: Runtime configuration, credentials, certificates, DLLs, logs, extracted data, bnetserver executable and character data

client_verification.scope: In response to the deployed-version cold-client login check, the user confirmed Krau entered the game on the first attempt.
client_verification.limitation: One successful client login does not establish that the intermittent handshake failure has been eliminated.

remaining_client_checks: Repeated client starts and ordinary logout/relog/instance transfers after the first successful cold-client login.
Preserve and trace any recurrence before restarting the client. Passing initializer probes or one successful login cannot prove the original intermittent silence permanently fixed.
Do not label this ownership/handoff repair a proven root-cause fix for the user's intermittent failure until actual client evidence supports that claim.
